quotes.text: Workflows are deterministic. Agents are probabilistic within boundaries. You define workflows, execute defined logic. Agents pursue defined intent. One requires instructions, the other requires supervision
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the core difference between agents and workflows into a memorable contrast.

quotes.text: Agents think, workflows act. The agent handles ambiguity interpreting language, weighing context, deciding intent. Once it reaches a confident conclusion, it delegates the mechanical execution to power automate.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the hybrid architecture where agents decide and workflows execute.

quotes.text: Use workflows when the process is repeatable, measurable, and legally or operationally intolerant of deviation. Use agents when the process requires interpretation, conversation, or decision making under uncertainty
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear decision rule for choosing between a workflow and an agent.

quotes.text: In governance terms, managing workflows is about inventory control, not behavioral oversight. You track what exists, who owns it, which connectors they're using, and how often they run.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies how governance of deterministic workflows differs from supervising agents.

takeaways: Power Automate workflows are deterministic rule execution, while Copilot Studio agents pursue goals and choose tools dynamically within defined boundaries.
Agents shift governance from inventory control and post-failure audits to supervising behavior, with the agent feed exposing what an agent did and why.
The most robust design is hybrid: agents interpret and decide, then delegate execution to auditable Power Automate workflows.
hook: Calling everything an AI automation hides a critical difference: a Power Automate workflow follows fixed steps, while a Copilot Studio agent reasons toward a goal and picks its own tools. This episode helps makers and Power Platform admins decide when to use workflows, agents or both, and how to keep governance intact as autonomy grows.
